title: Severe Allergic Reactions (Anaphylaxis)
source_note: PLACEHOLDER CONTENT — authored for prototype purposes. Replace with reviewed clinical source content before real deployment.
body: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that can develop within minutes of exposure to a trigger such as food, insect stings, medication, or latex.

Warning signs include swelling of the throat, tongue, or face, difficulty breathing or swallowing, widespread hives combined with swelling, a sudden drop in blood pressure, dizziness, or a feeling of impending doom.

If someone has a known severe allergy and carries an epinephrine auto-injector, it should be used immediately at the first sign of a severe reaction, followed immediately by a call to emergency services — epinephrine is time-critical and a second dose or additional care may still be needed even after symptoms improve.
